summary: This is the opening excerpt of a fiction piece titled "A Vessel for Offering" by Darren R. Hawkins, labeled as part 1 of Book 15. An unnamed man crawls through a cramped metal duct, dragging his body forward by his elbows while his flashlight wobbles and its strap comes loose. He is miserable about the stink, the heat, and especially the right-angle turns, which force his joints into unnatural positions. The passage combines physical struggle with dark humor and an inner sense of claustrophobia.
one_line: An unnamed man struggles through a stifling metal duct, cursing the right-angle turns, in the opening of Darren R. Hawkins's fiction piece "A Vessel for Offering."
key_facts: The excerpt is titled "A Vessel for Offering" by Darren R. Hawkins and is labeled Book 15, part 1.
The man is moving through ducts, vents and metal casements that thunder beneath his weight.
He advances by planting his elbows on a seam for traction and dragging his body behind him.
He has covered a few hundred meters of constant inchworm contractions through a space barely large enough for his shoulders.
His flashlight strap has been pulling loose for the last ten minutes and the beam keeps jiggling.
The air smells of sweat, dust, mildew and other assorted skanks rather than the clean copper stink of sheet metal and coolant.
He has been contorting his body for the last hour or better, using his pelvis, knee, elbow and sometimes neck.
He says he hates right angles most of all, because there are only so many joints in the human body capable of a ninety degree maneuver.
He compares himself to raw bratwurst crammed into sausage casings.
He is not normally one to give up in the face of grit, and the dirt and heat do not bother him as much as the intersections.
He imagines the plan's author deserving a citation, delivered with a hammer to the forehead.
A hysterically gibbering claustrophobe is chained up in a closet at the very back of his mind.
